*   **When to Use:** When rendering interactive volume visualizations on mobile devices with limited memory and processing power, and when visual fidelity can be sacrificed for speed [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the evidence supports using the described approach when rendering interactive volume visualizations on mobile devices with limited memory and processing power, and when visual fidelity can be sacrificed for speed. The source text explicitly describes an approach for accelerating 2D slicing volume visualization on mobile devices (specifically PDAs like DELL Axim) with limited resources (30 MB free memory). It details techniques such as adaptive screen-resolution rendering (rendering at lower resolution and scaling up), compressed palette textures, and single-texture uploads to manage memory. The text mentions that rendering at lower resolution reduces render time and that scaled images may contain blurred portions (sacrificing some fidelity) but achieves interactivity. The source confirms the context of mobile devices, limited memory/processing, and the trade-off between speed and fidelity (e.g., lower resolution, heuristic opacity estimation). Therefore, every fact in the claim is supported by the evidence.
